notes: Release 1.8.0

Browse: unsubscribing from a Workshop item in the app takes its mods out of the list and the profile, instead of leaving them on as "not installed" once Steam deletes them. Unsubscribing in Steam itself still keeps the row, so a mod gone for a while gets its place back

Publish: a translation draft the old Merger saved as glued objects is mended on the way (its objects joined into one, later keys winning), so a package that has one can still be published; only a .json that cannot be read at all is refused

Merger: adding a mod's block to a translation file joins its keys into the one JSON object (and taking it out removes them); a script file gets /* */ markers, only Lua gets --. Before, every file got Lua comments around a second copy, and a package's Translate/EN/UI.json held two JSON objects glued together. A publish now refuses a .json that is not one object, instead of shipping a file the game cannot read

Monitor: a require the game itself has under its Build 42 path is said to be only noise when nothing from that file fails afterwards (the game runs its own Lua before any mod's, so the module is there anyway); the card's text is in the app's language (it was the backend's English), and its button reads "Fix the path (only quiets the warning)". When the same file errors later in the log, the card says the path is what mends it
The Studio's rules and mod index live inside the app; nothing is downloaded and nothing is shared through GitHub any more

Monitor: a Java mod's own error ("[BloodFX] drawing disabled: java.lang.NullPointerException ...") gets its own card under the mod's name, without the Merger or a polyfill (neither reaches Java); the exception its stack trace repeats on the next line is not a second, anonymous card. Mod Health: a community-index require issue is left out once the mod as installed no longer has that require (ReactiveSE 1.3.0 moved ISUI/ISWorldMap itself, and the warning offered a compatible copy that would have brought the old file back)

Translate: the language of a text is the script with most letters (a description in Russian, Chinese and English said 'from Chinese' because any Han letter won). A 429 from Google stops at once instead of retrying every piece, MyMemory sends pieces joined up to its 500 bytes and refuses a too-long text before any call (it made 40 calls, then gave up), and the limit is explained in words with the DeepL way out

Mod Health: a mod id changed back by its author is caught too (RadioVoices -> RadioVoicesLocal -> RadioVoices today). The Studio now remembers which Workshop item each mod id was seen in (PZModStudio_Cache/mod_workshop_ids.json), so a missing id points to what its item holds now; for an id gone before it was noted, the one Workshop mod whose id starts it or is started by it. A new id already in the list is not offered (the old entry is just a leftover)

Novedades: 'Since you last played' shows the session's time, not only the date, and an empty list says when that session was and offers Last 7 days. A session at 18:54 read as 'since today' while today's earlier updates were left out

Novedades: the sidebar count is read again when the game enters or leaves a save, when the window comes back and on every tab change. Counted once at start, it kept showing 1 for an update the player had since played with, while the page (since the 18:54 session) rightly showed nothing

Monitor: Clear on the game console empties it for real; after a Clear on a full console (1500 lines) the tab stayed at 0 / 1502 forever, because it hid by line count and the rolling window never grew past it. Other tabs now hide up to the last line seen at Clear time

Launch: a windowed game that opens bigger than the screen is maximized (the game reopens at the size it saved maximized, title bar on top, so it ran under the taskbar); a window the player made smaller is left alone. Checked by the player on a real launch

Mod List: a not-installed mod taken out of the list (removed, or replaced by its new id) leaves the profile too, instead of coming back at the end; jumping to a mod outside the profile or hidden by a filter shows it (the panel fell back to the list's first mod). Reading the mod list only reconciles the Zomboid folder that holds the default.txt it read: with a temporary folder in the tests it fell through to the user's real one and rewrote its active profile with the test's mods
Mod List: a mod that is not installed shows one 'not installed' chip, the health check's (with its fix), not two

Mod Health: a mod whose author changed its id in an update is no longer 'unsubscribed or deleted'. When an installed folder is named like the missing id but holds another, the issue says so and offers to put the new id in the old one's place, switched on (RadioVoices became RadioVoicesLocal today; checked on the real list)
Mod List: the mod panel scrolls instead of squeezing its sections (a flex column shrank 'Mod data' to a sliver, so the scroll never appeared)

Steam downloads on every screen: a bar shows what Steam is downloading for the game (the items, queued / preparing / downloading / installing, MB and speed) and says when it is done, reading the mods again so the Mod List has them. Read from Steam's own logs and the bytes its process has written since the job started (Steam logs no progress and preallocates the files); no Steam API, so the player is never shown as in-game. Checked on a real download: 9.9 MB written for a 9.8 MB job

Shim: the place-item cursor no longer throws once its last item is placed (42.21's ISPlace3DItemCursor reads self.items[1] after create() removed it; isValid answers false and render/renderOpaqueObjectsInWorld do nothing on an empty list). The error Take A Bath was blamed for; checked in the game, wrapping once however often the shim runs

Mod List: Share to the index is gone (menu item, the For the index / In the index chips, the report pull request). It sent the Monitor's raw counts with a guessed owner and no fix, so the index got facts that were wrong or that the Studio already fixes; the index stays, curated by hand, and the app still reads it. The warn chip hides when the index has a known issue for the mod

Shim: Propane Explosion's aim check only with a ranged weapon (findAimTarget called getMaxRange on items that are not weapons; reproduced and checked in the game). Monitor: a card shows its own advice, and 'the shim covers this' only when it has none (the game's door code, which no Lua reaches, was told it was covered)

Shim: ModernStatus' auto-hidden indicators leave the screen again (42.21 clamps top-level UI to it, so 22 invisible ones sat at 0,0 taking the clicks over the primary-hand icon); checked in the game; ModernStatus in the index

Shim: Core:getKey(nil) answers nil without asking Java, which logged a NullPointerException each time (Fancy Handwork's key handler, hundreds a session); checked in the game; the index's Fancy Handwork entry says so

Link 1.18.3: the game's tooltips without the ghost box at the top-left (tick boxes, lists, combos... set their tooltip at a control-relative spot every frame, and it was drawn there before moving to the mouse); seen and checked in the game on sandbox options

Monitor: every Translator exception is the bare-% card (MissingFormatArgument and FormatFlagsConversionMismatch too), one card per mod whichever it threw; the MCP diagnostics fold per mod as the Monitor does
Mod List: chips laid right to left so the origin keeps the last column and the same chips line up; the warning count and In the index give way once the index knows the mod
Settings: Fetch now for the community files; the index and lists links open the site's mods page, not its home (also on the Workshop page)
Share: a registry the index's own check accepts (a compatible copy with no file named is fix none, mod.info incompatibilities say their source); the registries merged tonight brought in
Share: off while everything seen is in the index or a pull request; an issue proposed again replaces its entry in the registry instead of standing twice
Mod List: a mark on each mod with something for the community index (For the index / Something new / In the index), a tag to filter by it, and what was proposed remembered
Monitor: a bare % in a mod's texts names the mod (the key's owner), one card per mod, and counts toward that mod so it can be shared
